candidates.name: Trigeminal Neuralgia
support_spans: persistent severe pain on the left side of her face
episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain initially affecting the entire left hemiface
pain localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of severe, episodic, electric-shock–like pain in the trigeminal nerve distribution are classic for Trigeminal Neuralgia.

candidates.name: Multiple Sclerosis
support_spans: distorted sensations in the V2 region
contradict_spans: Routine laboratory tests, including D-dimer, were normal
RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and other infections was negative
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the head showed no abnormalities
candidates.why: The patient's distorted sensations could be indicative of a demyelinating disease like Multiple Sclerosis, but the lack of other neurological deficits and normal diagnostic tests make this less likely.

candidates.name: Vaccine-induced Trigeminal Neuralgia
support_spans: on the day after receiving her third dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, she experienced episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain
candidates.why: The temporal relationship between the vaccine administration and the onset of symptoms suggests a possible vaccine-induced cause of the patient's Trigeminal Neuralgia.
